# Computational Codebook & Reference Implementation {#sec-codebook}

## Software Architecture & Dependencies

This chapter provides a complete, production-grade computational reference implementation of the Survey-Weighted Dirichlet Process Mixture Model with Stratified Cluster Jackknife Variance Estimation and Affine Projection.

The pipeline combines high-performance C++ (`RcppArmadillo`) for the core MCMC iterations with modular R functions for survey calibration and affine projection.

### Setting the R Library Environment

On high-performance computing clusters (such as Longleaf), custom or user-installed packages should be prioritized by prepending the user library to `.libPaths()`:

```r
# Prepend personal R library if present
personal_lib <- "/nas/longleaf/home/aquijano/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.5"
if (dir.exists(personal_lib) && !(personal_lib %in% .libPaths())) {
  .libPaths(c(personal_lib, .libPaths()))
}

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(MASS)
  library(mvtnorm)
  library(label.switching)
  library(coda)
  library(Rcpp)
  library(RcppArmadillo)
})
```

## High-Performance C++ Sampling Kernel (`dpmm_helpers.cpp`)

The computationally demanding steps of the Gibbs sampler—computing multivariate Gaussian quadratic forms, evaluating log-sum-exp responsibilities, and updating Wishart matrices—are executed in C++ via `RcppArmadillo`.

```cpp
#include <RcppArmadillo.h>
// [[Rcpp::depends(RcppArmadillo)]]

using namespace Rcpp;
using namespace arma;

// [[Rcpp::export]]
IntegerVector sample_allocations_cpp(
    const mat& Y,
    const vec& pi,
    const mat& mu,
    const field<mat>& Sigma,
    int n,
    int L,
    int P
) {
  IntegerVector z(n);
  mat log_p(n, L);
  
  // Pre-invert and pre-determinant for each component
  field<mat> Sigma_inv(L);
  vec log_det_val(L);
  for (int k = 0; k < L; ++k) {
    mat S = Sigma(k);
    Sigma_inv(k) = inv_sympd(S);
    double val, sign;
    log_det(val, sign, S);
    log_det_val(k) = val;
  }
  
  // Compute unweighted responsibilities
  for (int k = 0; k < L; ++k) {
    vec m = mu.col(k);
    mat S_inv = Sigma_inv(k);
    double ldet = log_det_val(k);
    double lpi = std::log(std::max(pi(k), 1e-12));
    
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
      rowvec diff = Y.row(i) - m.t();
      double qf = as_scalar(diff * S_inv * diff.t());
      log_p(i, k) = lpi - 0.5 * ldet - 0.5 * qf;
    }
  }
  
  // Normalized Categorical draws
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    rowvec lp = log_p.row(i);
    double max_lp = max(lp);
    rowvec probs = exp(lp - max_lp);
    probs = probs / sum(probs);
    
    double u = R::runif(0.0, 1.0);
    double cum = 0.0;
    int chosen = L - 1;
    for (int k = 0; k < L; ++k) {
      cum += probs(k);
      if (u <= cum) {
        chosen = k;
        break;
      }
    }
    z[i] = chosen + 1; // 1-indexed for R
  }
  
  return z;
}
```

## Data-Driven Merging & Threshold Consolidation

When true component centroids and $K_0$ are unknown, the unit-level partition is estimated from the posterior similarity matrix via `mcclust::maxpear`, followed by iterative threshold consolidation:

```r
#' Consolidate Small or Close Cluster Fragments
#' @param z Integer vector of cluster assignments (length n)
#' @param Y Matrix of continuous biomarker manifest variables (n x P)
#' @param w Normalized survey weights (length n, sum(w) = n)
#' @param min_weight_frac Minimum weight fraction required for an independent cluster (default 0.02)
#' @param min_sep Minimum Euclidean centroid distance required between distinct clusters (default 1.5)
#' @return Consolidated cluster assignment vector with contiguous labels 1..K_final
merge_small_close_groups <- function(z, Y, w, min_weight_frac = 0.02, min_sep = 1.5) {
  total_w <- sum(w)
  repeat {
    groups <- sort(unique(z))
    K <- length(groups)
    if (K <= 1) break

    wt <- sapply(groups, function(g) sum(w[z == g]))
    centroids <- t(sapply(groups, function(g) {
      idx <- which(z == g)
      colSums(Y[idx, , drop = FALSE] * w[idx]) / sum(w[idx])
    }))

    dmat <- as.matrix(dist(centroids))
    diag(dmat) <- Inf

    # Condition 1: Merge satellite clusters with < min_weight_frac into nearest neighbor
    smallest_idx <- which.min(wt)
    if (wt[smallest_idx] / total_w < min_weight_frac) {
      g_small  <- groups[smallest_idx]
      g_target <- groups[which.min(dmat[smallest_idx, ])]
      z[z == g_small] <- g_target
      next
    }

    # Condition 2: Merge pairs of clusters closer than min_sep
    min_pair <- which(dmat == min(dmat), arr.ind = TRUE)[1, ]
    if (dmat[min_pair[1], min_pair[2]] < min_sep) {
      z[z == groups[min_pair[2]]] <- groups[min_pair[1]]
      next
    }
    break
  }
  match(z, sort(unique(z)))  # Relabel to contiguous 1..K_final
}
```

## Analytical Profile Hessian & Score Functions


The marginal profile score vector and observed information bread matrix are computed directly from the sub-mixture density matrix `a_mat`:

```r
#' Compute Analytical Profile Hessian and Sample Score
#' @param a_mat Matrix of sub-mixture densities (n x K0)
#' @param pi_bar Current prevalence vector (length K0)
#' @param weights Survey weights (length n, normalized to sum(w) = n)
#' @return List containing H_hat ((K0-1) x (K0-1)) and score_mat (n x (K0-1))
compute_profile_hessian_and_scores <- function(a_mat, pi_bar, weights) {
  n <- nrow(a_mat)
  K0 <- ncol(a_mat)
  K_free <- K0 - 1
  
  # Marginal mixture density per unit
  m_i <- as.vector(a_mat %*% pi_bar)
  m_i <- pmax(m_i, 1e-12) # Protect against underflow
  
  # Contrasts against reference category K0
  diff_mat <- a_mat[, 1:K_free, drop = FALSE] - a_mat[, K0]
  
  # Individual score contributions: w_i * (a_ik - a_iK0) / m_i
  score_mat <- (weights / m_i) * diff_mat
  
  # Analytical profile Hessian: H_hat = sum_i w_i * diff_i * diff_i' / m_i^2
  w_scaled <- weights / (m_i^2)
  H_hat <- matrix(0, nrow = K_free, ncol = K_free)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    d_i <- diff_mat[i, ]
    H_hat <- H_hat + w_scaled[i] * tcrossprod(d_i)
  }
  
  list(H_hat = H_hat, score_mat = score_mat)
}
```

## Stratified Delete-PSU Jackknife Implementation

The deterministic delete-PSU jackknife routine calculates the meat matrix $J_{\text{jack}}$ across all strata and clusters:

```r
#' Stratified Delete-PSU Jackknife for Marginal Score
#' @param a_mat Matrix of sub-mixture densities (n x K0)
#' @param pi_bar Current prevalence vector (length K0)
#' @param weights Survey design weights
#' @param strata Stratum indicator vector
#' @param clusters Cluster (PSU) indicator vector
#' @return The calibrated meat matrix J_jack ((K0-1) x (K0-1))
compute_jackknife_meat <- function(a_mat, pi_bar, weights, strata, clusters) {
  K0 <- ncol(a_mat)
  K_free <- K0 - 1
  m_i <- as.vector(a_mat %*% pi_bar)
  diff_mat <- a_mat[, 1:K_free, drop = FALSE] - a_mat[, K0]
  
  unique_strata <- unique(strata)
  H <- length(unique_strata)
  M_total <- length(unique(interaction(strata, clusters)))
  df_design <- M_total - H
  c_corr <- M_total / df_design
  
  J_raw <- matrix(0, nrow = K_free, ncol = K_free)
  
  for (h in unique_strata) {
    stratum_mask <- (strata == h)
    psu_in_stratum <- unique(clusters[stratum_mask])
    n_h <- length(psu_in_stratum)
    
    if (n_h <= 1) next
    
    # Calculate replicate scores S_(hc)
    rep_scores <- matrix(0, nrow = n_h, ncol = K_free)
    for (c_idx in seq_along(psu_in_stratum)) {
      c_val <- psu_in_stratum[c_idx]
      w_rep <- weights
      
      # Re-weighting: omitted PSU gets 0, remaining PSUs get n_h / (n_h - 1)
      omit_mask <- stratum_mask & (clusters == c_val)
      keep_mask <- stratum_mask & (clusters != c_val)
      
      w_rep[omit_mask] <- 0
      w_rep[keep_mask] <- weights[keep_mask] * (n_h / (n_h - 1))
      
      # Score contribution
      rep_scores[c_idx, ] <- colSums((w_rep / m_i) * diff_mat)
    }
    
    # Stratum center
    mean_s_h <- colMeans(rep_scores)
    
    # Add stratum variance contribution
    diff_s_h <- sweep(rep_scores, 2, mean_s_h, "-")
    J_h <- ((n_h - 1) / n_h) * crossprod(diff_s_h)
    J_raw <- J_raw + J_h
  }
  
  # Return design degrees-of-freedom scaled meat matrix
  c_corr * J_raw
}
```

## Total-Variance Recombination & Affine Projection

This function executes the total-variance recombination and performs the affine Cholesky transformation on MCMC draws:

```r
#' Total-Variance Recombination and Affine Projection
#' @param draws_free MCMC draws matrix (M x (K0-1))
#' @param H_hat Profile Hessian matrix ((K0-1) x (K0-1))
#' @param J_jack Jackknife meat matrix ((K0-1) x (K0-1))
#' @return Affine-rotated draws on full simplex (M x K0)
affine_project_draws <- function(draws_free, H_hat, J_jack) {
  M <- nrow(draws_free)
  K_free <- ncol(draws_free)
  K0 <- K_free + 1
  
  # 1. Godambe Sandwich Covariance
  H_inv <- solve(H_hat)
  Sigma_sandwich <- H_inv %*% J_jack %*% H_inv
  
  # 2. Naive Empirical MCMC Covariance
  Sigma_naive <- cov(draws_free)
  
  # 3. Total-Variance Recombination
  Sigma_corrected <- Sigma_sandwich + Sigma_naive
  
  # 4. Cholesky Factorizations
  R1 <- chol(Sigma_corrected) # R1' R1 = Sigma_corrected
  R2 <- chol(Sigma_naive)     # R2' R2 = Sigma_naive
  
  # Affine rotation operator A = R2^{-1} R1
  A <- solve(R2, R1)
  
  # 5. Transform Draws
  mean_free <- colMeans(draws_free)
  centered <- sweep(draws_free, 2, mean_free, "-")
  rotated_free <- centered %*% A
  rotated_free <- sweep(rotated_free, 2, mean_free, "+")
  
  # 6. Reconstruct Full Simplex
  full_draws <- matrix(0, nrow = M, ncol = K0)
  full_draws[, 1:K_free] <- rotated_free
  full_draws[, K0] <- 1 - rowSums(rotated_free)
  
  # Simplex boundary protection (Euclidean projection if needed)
  for (m in seq_len(M)) {
    if (any(full_draws[m, ] < 0) || any(full_draws[m, ] > 1)) {
      full_draws[m, ] <- pmax(full_draws[m, ], 0)
      full_draws[m, ] <- full_draws[m, ] / sum(full_draws[m, ])
    }
  }
  
  full_draws
}
```

## Execution Guide

### SLURM Batch Execution on HPC Clusters

To execute the model estimation on a SLURM cluster:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=dpmm_survey
#SBATCH --output=logs/dpmm_%A_%a.out
#SBATCH --error=logs/dpmm_%A_%a.err
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=1
#SBATCH --mem=4G
#SBATCH --time=02:00:00
#SBATCH --array=1-1000%50

module load r/4.5.0

# Set user R library
export R_LIBS_USER="/nas/longleaf/home/aquijano/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.5"

# Run replicate
Rscript simulations/src/R/dpmm_fit.R --replicate=${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}
```

This completes the fully self-contained reference implementation.
